value: acceleration threshold declined with falling frequency below 10 Hz, to close to 1e-5 m/s2 at 0.1 Hz
eye: whole-animal conditioned heart-rate response to infrasound in a standing-wave acoustic tube
method: cardiac conditioning: a stimulus of 10 to 20 s ended with a mild electric shock (4 V a.c.) to the tail; a response was scored when a heart-beat interval during the stimulus exceeded the longest of the 20 preceding intervals by at least 10 %
conditions: 11 cod, 31 to 34 cm long, tested in the tube; all were conditioned to 3 or 10 Hz but only six individuals were trainable to the lower frequencies, so the 0.1 Hz end rests on at most six fish; water temperature not stated; thresholds by a staircase in 3 dB steps at 50 % response probability, averaged over 2 to 3 days per frequency, reported as mean ± S.D.; the authors attribute detection to the otolith organs but did not block the lateral line

source.title: Detection of Infrasound By The Atlantic Cod

quote: The threshold values, measured as particle acceleration, showed a steady decline towards lower frequencies below 10 Hz, reaching a value close to 10-5 m s-2 at 0.1 Hz.
note: The authors write that they could not measure the background acceleration noise in the tube at these frequencies and that the thresholds might be masked by it, so the shape of the audiogram may in part reflect that noise; they call the generally high sensitivity to infrasound the biologically important result. The PDF text layer prints the units and the 0.1 as garbled characters; the value was checked against the journal page abstract, which prints 10-5 m s-2 at 0.1 Hz. Name: GBIF species match ACCEPTED; Catalog of Fishes not opened.

value: heat receptor RpTRPA5B: mean activation threshold 53 C (open probability 0.1), T0.5 58.6 C, saturating at 68 C, in vitro
eye: heterologously expressed heat-activated ion channel (molecular), not a whole-animal threshold
method: whole-cell patch clamp of HEK293T cells expressing RpTRPA5B, membrane held at -30 mV, optical heat pulses and temperature steps; threshold defined as Po = 0.1 from van't Hoff plots
conditions: in vitro only; the paper does not show RpTRPA5B function in vivo or its location in peripheral sensory neurons; only TRPA5B was tested, the paralogs RpTRPA5A and RpTRPA5C were not; temperature seemed a partial activator (maximal open probability lower than in control channels); no n stated in the Figure 2 legend

source.authors: Liénard MA, Baez-Nieto D, Tsai C-C, Valencia-Montoya WA, Werin B, Johanson U, Lassance J-M, Pan JQ, Yu N, Pierce NE
source.title: TRPA5 encodes a thermosensitive ankyrin ion channel receptor in a triatomine insect

quote: The average temperature for the activation “threshold” was 53°C, defined as Po = 0.1 calculated from the van’t Hoff plots.
note: T0.5 = 58.6 C and saturation at 68 C (Po = 0.9) come from the next sentence of the Results, not from the quote. Channel activation is noxious-range (the abstract compares it with noxious TRPV receptors in mammals) and kinetics are slow, so this is a heat-pain-range receptor property, not a behavioural thermal preference. Authors listed per Crossref; CC BY 4.0. Name: GBIF species match ACCEPTED. The Discussion notes that activation above 50 C may lie outside the bug's ecological temperature preferences and cites an upper thermal tolerance of R. prolixus of 50.5 C, below this channel's threshold.
